selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What does the palace stand for in the comparison?
questions.answer: It stands for this world.

questions.question: Who is described as the ruler of this palace-like world?
questions.answer: Allah is the ruler.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah by describing Him as ruler over heavens and earth?
questions.answer: It teaches that He has complete rule and power over all creation.

questions.question: What does the stove and kitchen of the palace represent?
questions.answer: It represents the earth, which has fire inside it and produces things on its surface.

questions.question: What do the foods in the comparison help us think about in the world?
questions.answer: They help us think about Allah’s blessings and provision.

questions.question: What real thing is represented by the stove and kitchen?
questions.answer: The earth.

questions.question: How are animals described in relation to human beings here?
questions.answer: They are described as serving human beings.

questions.question: Who are his students?
questions.answer: The saints and purified scholars.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the believing group?
questions.answer: They are people of faith who learn from the Qur’an.

questions.question: What is the believing group connected to?
questions.answer: They are connected to faith and the guidance of the Qur’an.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of this passage after the story ends?
questions.answer: It explains the real meaning behind the comparison.

questions.question: What part of the palace matches the heavens?
questions.answer: The roof.

questions.question: What does the palace floor correspond to?
questions.answer: The earth.

questions.question: What example of order in the universe is given in the passage?
questions.answer: The changing of night and day is given as a sign of His rule.

questions.question: What do the palace’s amazing crafts represent?
questions.answer: They represent the wonders of Allah’s power in the world.

questions.question: What are the many rooms of the palace compared to?
questions.answer: The many worlds or realms in creation.

questions.question: Why are angels compared to servants in the palace?
questions.answer: Because they carry out Allah’s commands in the world.

questions.question: What is the job of the prophets in relation to the master in this passage?
questions.answer: They help guide people as his assistants in the same mission of truth.

questions.question: Which creatures are called guests in the world?
questions.answer: Jinn, people, and animals.

questions.question: What two bad influences do they follow?
questions.answer: Satan and their lower selves.

questions.question: What does the passage say the palace really is?
questions.answer: It is the world we live in.

questions.question: What does the shining roof of the palace represent?
questions.answer: The sky filled with stars.

questions.question: What do the amazing arts in the palace point to in the real meaning?
questions.answer: They point to Allah’s powerful works and wonders in the world.

questions.question: What are the palace rooms compared to?
questions.answer: They are compared to many different worlds or levels of creation.

title: Transition to Reality Application of the Palace to the World and Statement of the Two Parties
